claims.scope: One physical RNG, IRQ 64, internal entropy/conditioning block; no pad route, executable RNG profile, entropy certification, cryptographic suitability or observed recovery admitted.

finite_source_maps.qualification: Widths and reset values are literal source data, not an allowed Cartesian configuration. HTCR3 map typo retained separately. Only recommended health configurations have described behavior.

kernel_clock.qualification: Source readiness, rate, shared ownership and CLKDIV sampling constraints are independent gates.

literal_configurations.qualification: Literal field comparison: SDK candidate NIST equals RM C fields, GermanBSI equals RM B. No certified configuration A is supplied here; AN4230 and certification records were not inspected. RM783 vendor validation used rng_clk=48 MHz and CED=0. Configuration C CLKDIV=5 is the tabulated 48 MHz case; RM784 note3 requires adapting CLKDIV for another RNG clock and limits noise sampling to 48 MHz or less.

contracts.detail: AHB clocks registers and conditioning. Shared RNG/USB CK48SEL[25:24] selects 1=PSIDIV3, 2=HSIDIV3, 3=HSE; reset 0 disables the kernel clock. Check selected source readiness and rate, including HSIDIV3RDY/PSIDIV3RDY; both divided sources stop in Stop/Standby. HSE supported range can reach 50 MHz, so source selection alone does not enforce the 48 MHz noise-sampling ceiling after CLKDIV. Own the shared selector with USB and validate effective sampling rate. With CED=0, pre-divider RNG frequency must exceed HCLK/32; equality is not positively admitted. Only single 32-bit accesses are documented; other sizes cause bus error and ignored writes.

FIFO holds four words with a further conditioning output potentially available. Check status and DRDY before reads. A zero DR value is a seed-error indicator requiring error handling, not a value to silently skip. DR reads consume shared state, including with RNGEN=0 and buffered data. No speculative DR polling, debugger auto-refresh or competing consumers.

Startup repetition/adaptive tests and conditioning known-answer checks precede output; continuous tests monitor noise. Default described thresholds are repetition beyond 28 equal bits and adaptive first-bit count beyond 684 in 1024 bits. SECS/CECS are current status; SEIS/CEIS record errors and clear on zero writes. Clock-error data must not be used. HTSR error evidence clears with SEIS; capture before clearing. Health success alone does not establish entropy certification. The 28 and 684/1024 thresholds describe reset HTCR0=0x72AC, not recommended 0xAAC7; RM789 does not guarantee behavior, including reads, for other than its recommended value. CECS is valid only with CED=0; CED=1 disables clock-error detection.

Before CONDRST, clear RNGEN and wait BUSY = 0. Set correct CR configuration with CONDRST in the same access; clear CONDRST and await completion. CONDRST explicitly clears all FIFOs and RNG_SR but preserves configuration registers. RCC reset loses recommended configuration. CONFIGLOCK blocks configuration until RNG reset and restricts recovery; it is not a releasable mutex. Separate HTSR freshness across CONDRST is not explicitly established by that sentence; RM790 specifies clearing SEIS clears HTSR.

Before clock gating or a power mode deactivating RNG: clear RNGEN, await BUSY = 0, then gate. Disabled RNG can retain readable buffered output; disabling during initialization can pause and later resume it. RNGEN = 0 alone is not clean-buffer or quiescence evidence.

Seed recovery depends on ARDIS and CONFIGLOCK. RM describes oscillator error accumulation/masking, recommended at least six active oscillators for N >= 3, conditional B-to-C transition and final SECS checks. ES2.5.1 requires correct standard error management; API presence does not prove successful recovery. Unexpected tamper errors stop output and require peripheral reset plus initialization; seed errors are not tamper events.

IE globally enables DRDY, CEIS and SEIS sources. Data-ready status drains through data consumption; error clear and buffer ownership must be coordinated. Polling, IRQ and other consumers cannot independently own the same FIFO or status provenance.

RM describes 206*N AHB cycles or 128*N effective RNG cycles per four-word set, depending on the limiting stage. This is conditional vendor timing, not measured throughput, initialization deadline or entropy validation; CLKDIV affects sampling frequency.

RM787 also sets BUSY when a connected peripheral fetches random data through the dedicated RNG hardware bus. Whether an exact C542 consumer is present remains unverified; no such route is admitted and CPU ownership alone is not generalized into a hardware-bus proof.

source_derived_SDK_gates.detail: SetConfig uses debug-only width/enumeration checks and unmasked shifts; health_test is written directly. Width acceptance does not establish a recommended configuration. Additional health index is debug-checked, with LL indexing HTCR directly. Optional runtime checks do not validate the complete domain; independently bound pointers, indices, values and combinations. For example config_1 bit11 shifts into CONFIGLOCK bit31, bits8/9 into reserved28/29, config_3 bit4 into NISTC and config_2 bit3 into CLKDIV. LL HTCR indexing outside 0..3 is out-of-bounds C access; nominal address arithmetic places index4/5 at HTSR,6/7 at reserved offsets and8 at NSMR, not a guaranteed compiled write. The noise-source predicate admits three selected oscillators, which does not establish the recommended six for N>=3.

SetConfig waits BUSY but does not first disable RNGEN; granular CED/ARDIS/divider and health setters do not implement the full RNGEN/BUSY reset preflight or completion wait. Handle IDLE is not hardware quiescence. LL setters pulse CONDRST and can discard buffered entropy; preserve ownership and exact sequence. Candidate B/C functions likewise wait BUSY without first clearing RNGEN and overwrite CR with CONDRST, forcing IE, ARDIS and CED to zero.

Polling clears CEIS and continues without rejecting persistent CECS, despite RM forbidding clock-error data use. Polling and IRQ inner read loops store DR words without the RM nonzero check and without rechecking all health status for each word. Conditional source gap; no observed defective output claimed. CECS only has documented validity with CED=0; disabling the detector is not proof of a healthy clock. Both paths clear SEIS without first capturing HTSR and can destroy diagnostic evidence.

Polling can partially write the output buffer before seed error or timeout and provides no returned count. Final elapsed-time test can return timeout even after the last requested word was stored. The inner DRDY/count loop does not check the deadline per word. Tick progression and buffer extent require caller ownership; discard or explicitly track uncertain partial results.

IT start stores pointer/count and enables interrupts without stale-flag clearing. Handler has no ACTIVE, IE or positive-count preflight. Conditional on reaching its DRDY loop after a completed transfer, retained pointer is one-past-buffer and count=0: the next source-level write is outside that buffer and decrement wraps to 0xFFFFFFFF. After Init p_data is NULL, so an equivalent manual/stale invocation can dereference NULL. C undefined behavior and actual generated execution are unqualified; no corruption observed. Clock-error callback precedes data loop, requiring reentrancy control. SEIS set with SECS clear calls error callback and returns without draining or recording SEED; it may leave ACTIVE and needs renewed-delivery analysis.

DeInit only disables RNGEN and marks RESET. It does not disable IE, await BUSY, reset pointer/count, clear flags or flush output. Polling also does not neutralize inherited IE. Stale NVIC/IRQ and competing consumers must be drained before buffer or clock release.

RecoverSeedError is explicitly caller-invoked. It enables RNG, uses empirical tick deadlines, can return HAL_ERROR when final SECS remains set, and can leave RNG enabled on final return. Its aggregate overlap counter over ORed health bits is not independently demonstrated equivalent to RM per-oscillator accumulated counts. CondReset writes need RM preflight verification; successful return is not certified entropy recovery or a completed adapter. The fewer-than-six branch passes NOISE_SRC_1|2|3=0x7 to GetOscNoiseSrc, returning NSCR&7; with NSCR=0x1FF it writes NSMR=7, selecting only three oscillators. The other branch passes OSC_1|2|3=0x1FF. CLKDIV<5 is used as a proxy for configuration B; the C switch overwrites whole CR with 0x08451F00|CONDRST, forcing IE/ARDIS/CED=0 and CLKDIV=5 regardless of input clock. With SECS=1 and both HTSR=0, the reset body is skipped until timeout; locked configuration skips recovery and reaches final error if SECS persists. There is no explicit SEIS clear in that loop, but CONDRST does clear RNG_SR per RM785; HTSR freshness still needs qualification. Timeout is empirical 1+2^CLKDIV/4 ms (1,9,8193 at raw0,5,15).

On final SECS failure, optional last_error_codes uses &= HAL_RNG_ERROR_SEED, not |=; this can retain zero if SEED was absent and drops other error bits. Return status and independent captured health evidence are required; no observed execution claimed.

Configuration reset wait marks IDLE on timeout as well as success; IDLE does not prove BUSY = 0. Lock uses a tick timeout after write, so timeout alone does not prove configuration remains unlocked. Timeouts require a progressing timebase; no timeout is a rollback.

conflicts.detail: RM777 calls the clock too slow but describes an RNG cycle smaller than AHB cycle / 32; RM780 and SR descriptions specify RNG frequency below HCLK / 32. Preserve incompatible period wording; use no boundary admission from the typo.
RM786 introductory divider range says 1 to 16, but explicit encodings are 2^raw through 32768; SDK constants follow powers of two. Preserve prose discrepancy.

Exact header candidate NIST CR decodes to RM configuration C, while RM784 says only configuration A is suitable for NIST-compliant key generation and delegates A to AN4230. Candidate API naming and NISTC field naming do not establish certification. Separately HAL_RNG_NIST equals LL_RNG_NIST_COMPLIANT=0, meaning NISTC=0/default N=2 with CONFIG3 ignored, not B or C. This enum name also does not certify output.

RM792 prints HTCR3 offset 0x01F and RNG_MSMR; RM789 formula 0x010 + 4*x and exact header array put HTCR3 at 0x01C, and RM791/header name NSMR. Preserve table transcription discrepancies. Exact header also comments NSMR as a health test status register; its named mask behavior follows RM791, not that comment.
LL Set/GetConfig1 comments describe six bits / 0x3F, while exact header and RM field are eight bits and HAL guard allows 0xFF. No six-bit hardware restriction inferred.

RM788 says DRDY clears upon DR read and describes emptying the buffer; RM776/779 describe four plus potentially four output reads per ready period. HAL rechecks DRDY for each word. Preserve this tension without assuming a fixed number of reads per flag.

RM776 describes DRDY rising-transition interrupt, RM786 pending while flag set, RM783 interrupts only when enabled, and RM788 permits DRDY set after RNGEN clears. Re-delivery after auto-recovered SEIS early return is unresolved; an edge-only interpretation could leave transfer pending. No observed stall claimed.
RM781 recovery steps do not explicitly include the separate RNGEN=0 and BUSY=0 preflight required by RM785 before CONDRST. Preserve both and require the stricter preflight in any eventual adapter.

errata_gate.detail: Continuous seed errors can arise under supply, temperature and process combinations. ES calls for correct standard error management; no independently qualified recovery or entropy output here.

family_exclusion.detail: RM268 explicitly limits its cryptographic subsystem clock/reset subsection to C59x/5A3. Do not import the Figure28 multi-peripheral clock topology or its subsystem-wide reset sequence as an exact C542 rule. RNG chapter BUSY-before-clock-gate requirement still applies independently.
